messages:
sam_support: Heads-up — customer acme-corp is seeing a spike of 504s on hosted inference. ~09:12 UTC we started getting >1k 504s/min on /v1/generate. Raising support ticket #12345. Sample repro curl and response below.

sam_support: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \ 
  -d '{"model":"xlarge-td", "input":"<long prompt>"}'

HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "request timed out waiting for queue to drain"
}
```

kevin_sre: thanks. do we have ingress/gateway logs for that tenant/time? any sign of retry amplification or long KV loads? @maria_infra can you pull queue_depth and batcher_backlog metrics for the node pool serving hosted-gateway?

sam_support: attaching short log snippet from 09:11–09:15 UTC: 

sam_support: ```
level=warn ts=2026-03-17T09:12:03Z component=ingress msg="early-reject" tenant=acme-corp queue_depth=1024 limit=1000 reason="queue_depth_exceeded"
level=error ts=2026-03-17T09:12:05Z component=batcher msg="request-timeout" request_id=req-abc123 duration_ms=30005
level=warn ts=2026-03-17T09:12:06Z component=kvcache msg="kvcache-miss" tenant=acme-corp key=ctx:large_seq
```

maria_infra: looks like queue depth hit the configured cap and early-rejects started. batching backlog spiked — continuous-batcher queue length jumped from 120 -> 1800 in <1m. autoscaler did not add nodes; investigating why scale-up didn't trigger.

carol_eng: are these long-sequence requests (big token counts) or many short ones? that affects batching and KV warmup. can we get sample token counts and any client-side retry behavior?

sam_support: confirmed long requests (avg ~12k tokens) and the client did aggressive retries on 5xx. tenant traffic pattern changed ~09:10 when a nightly job began sending bulk document summarization.

deploy-bot: config-change: gateway.queue_depth_limit=1000 rolled out to hosted-gateway-canary @ 07:15 UTC (pr #4521).

kevin_sre: that config rollback likely explains the regression — we previously had dynamic headroom for bursts. two immediate mitigations: 1) raise gateway.queue_depth_limit to 2000 for hosted-gateway (temporary), 2) enable per-tenant emergency throttling to shed retries. Maria, can you lift the limit and watch p95? Carol, prepare a fallback model (smaller context) for acme-corp.

maria_infra: raising limit to 2000 on the live pool now (manual override). watching metrics — continuous-batcher backlog is dropping, p95 tail latency falling from 18s -> 3s. will keep for 15m then plan safe rollback.

carol_eng: creating canary smaller-model route and a rollout plan to redirect tenant to xlarge-td-smol if backlog reappears. also adding a prompt-length precheck to reject >8k tokens with helpful 4xx so we avoid long-tail blocking.

ops-oncall: filing incident and escalation: INC-2026-457. action items: collect full pprof traces from batcher hot shards, capture retry histogram from gateway, and ask acme-corp to pause the nightly job.

sam_support: notified acme-corp support contact (PM) and asked them to throttle/pause while we stabilize. they confirmed pause in ~5m.

kevin_sre: follow-up (post-mortem) asks: why autoscaler didn't add capacity (observability/alerting gap), ensure queue_depth_limit rollouts default to conservative canary windows, add per-tenant burst-shed policy.

maria_infra: agreed. I'll open infra-issue for autoscaler tuning and a dashboard alert if queue_depth > 70% for >1m.

carol_eng: I'll own the fallback route + precheck task. tagging for post-mortem notes.

sam_support: thanks — closing the immediate escalation, monitoring for 30m. :thumbsup:
